summary: This session contains 13 reviewed changes. They span the files recorded in the changes. In short, Team instructions now allow automated helpers to run / Web interface switches to dusk dark look with / Pages now share soft rounded dusk cards with / This update rewrites the project documents to replace / This change adds mapping for captured sessions cleans; and 8 more.

changes.title: Housekeeping rules and styling tweak
changes.summary: The team instruction sheet now lets automated helpers install packages on their own and only ask you for a command when something fails or looks risky. The code formatting settings now understand website styling directives so those files check cleanly.
before: Helpers had to hand you every install command and wait.
Styling files with special website directives could trip the formatter check.
now: Helpers can run installs themselves and fall back to your help only when needed, with a reminder to log finished work.
Those styling directives are now accepted, so checks stay quiet with no change to how the site looks.

files.note: Updated helper rules for installs and work logging.
Allowed website styling directives in formatter checks.

changes.digest: Team instructions now allow automated helpers to run package installs themselves and only hand over a one line command when an install fails or looks risky while adding a reminder to read the build tracker before work and log each finished unit afterwards without editing others and formatting settings now accept website styling directives so style checks stay clean with no change to what users see or how pages behave in this small housekeeping update

The file view always showed the latest snapshot and visited hunks had no mark.
now: Panels, header, and pages use the dusk colors, fonts, and wider spacing.
The file view follows the scrub time when given, and visited hunks show an opened label.

changes.title: Ownership checks replace puzzle questions
changes.summary: The documents now describe understanding checks as ownership questions about real changes instead of small coding puzzles. Open answers are judged against a checklist with quoted support, while breakage questions still use isolated runs to establish ground truth. Recent progress notes and visual direction wording are updated to match.
before: Checks were described as predict-the-output and spot-the-bug puzzles graded by running code.
now: Checks are described as ownership questions about consequences, decisions, tradeoffs, breakage, and teaching back.

changes.title: Safer sandbox output reading
changes.summary: The helper that reads the first line of tool output now accepts missing output and returns an empty result instead of failing. This keeps backend detection steady when version or inspection commands produce no text.
before: Reading command output assumed text was always present, so missing output could break the check.
now: Missing output now safely becomes an empty line, so detection continues and reports availability cleanly.

changes.title: Safe runs, project identity, change views
changes.summary: The small built-in code runner now actually runs snippets in an isolated space with limited memory, time, and output instead of reporting as unavailable. Snapshots can now recognize which project a folder belongs to and show line-by-line changes between saved states, and review helpers for reading patches are now shared.
before: The built-in runner always reported itself as missing, so no code could run there.
Snapshots had no shared way to tie a subfolder to its project or to show what changed between saves.
now: Snippets run safely with console output captured, overlong output trimmed, and timeouts or errors reported clearly.
Working folders now join their main project, saved states can be compared as plain change text, and patch reading helpers are available to others.

changes.title: Session review with change history
changes.summary: Readers now get an assembled review for a session that turns saved file snapshots and past events into ranked changes with evidence. Log intake was reworked to read only new data and record snapshots, while the web client gained calls for reviews, stories, history, and checks.
before: Sessions stored snapshots and events but had no single review explaining final changes and earlier attempts.
The web client could only list projects, sessions, events, and snapshot files.
now: A session can now show final edits, per-file attempts including reverted work, and linked evidence for each change.
Log intake tails files incrementally and the web client can request reviews, stories, history, and checks.
howItWorks: Collects all snapshots for the session and picks the starting and ending file states for comparison.
Compares file versions across time to mark each attempt as starting, replaced, or landed and to trace final lines back to the snapshot that introduced them.
Ranks the final edits by importance and attaches nearby tool uses and messages as supporting evidence.
Falls back to a diagnostic needing two snapshots when there is not enough history, keeping uncertain files marked uncertain.

files.note: Reworks log intake to tail new bytes and record snapshots and checkpoints.
Adds coverage for linking final edits to earlier and reverted snapshots.
Builds the ranked session review with attempts and evidence.
Adds web requests for reviews, stories, history, checks, and engagement.

changes.digest: Added deterministic session review that compares baseline and final snapshots maps each final line to its origin ranks hunks and links tool and message evidence while ingest now tails logs from checkpoints records snapshots and reconciles quietly and web client gains review story history and checks calls for richer reading without changing stored data formats

changes.title: Track file attempts across review history
changes.summary: This change adds a review index that reads file change comparisons and explains what happened to every saved version. Each version is labeled with a clear outcome, such as landed, reverted, replaced, or uncertain, plus how much text survived to the end.
before: There was no shared way to read change comparisons and explain what happened to each file version.
now: Change comparisons are now read directly, and each file version is labeled with what survived to the end, like landed, reverted, replaced, or uncertain.
Matching change blocks now get stable identity even when trailing spaces differ.
howItWorks: Read change comparison text into per-file lists of added, removed, and unchanged lines, rejecting blocks that disagree with their header.
Treat trailing spaces as meaningless when comparing blocks so identical edits share one identity.
Compare each saved version line by line against the final file to count introduced and surviving lines and locate where they landed.
Label each version as starting point, landed, partly landed, reverted, replaced, failed, or uncertain when its text was missing.

files.note: Adds tests covering parsing, identity, and attempt outcomes.
Adds review index for parsing diffs and tracking file attempts.

changes.digest: Adds review index that parses unified diffs for added deleted and changed files validates hunk bodies normalizes trailing whitespace for stable identities tracks each file version against final text labels attempts as baseline landed reverted replaced or uncertain and records surviving lines replacement text origins and evidence links with thorough tests guarding parsing identity and lifecycle outcomes

changes.title: Sessions join repository projects correctly
changes.summary: Sessions that start in a subfolder are now grouped under their repository's shared project instead of splitting by folder. The allowed folder list still controls which work gets captured, so nearby folders stay out unless enabled.
before: Sessions were matched by direct folder, so subfolder work could miss its repository home and sibling folders risked mixing.
now: Subfolder work now lands under one stable repository project, unrelated siblings are skipped, and quiet sessions can trigger a background story summary.
howItWorks: Find the repository and remote for where the session ran to pick one shared project.
Check that the starting folder sits inside the allowed list before capturing anything.
Save the session tape and snapshots under that shared project storage.
When a session goes quiet, start a story summary in the background without slowing or stopping capture.

changes.title: Projects join by repository address
changes.summary: Projects are now identified by their shared remote repository address when one exists, so the same code counts as one project even from different folders or machines. Session imports can accept a server-chosen project identity, and the shared data shapes now carry richer project, session, and review details.
before: Each local folder made its own separate project identity, so subfolders and different checkouts stayed split.
now: Equivalent repository addresses collapse to one project, with the local folder used only when no remote is known.
howItWorks: Cleaning of repository addresses removes differences in login details, ports, slashes, and endings so matching code maps together.
A repository identity is resolved from the main folder and cleaned remote, producing one stable project identifier.
Incoming sessions use the server-provided project when available and otherwise fall back to folder identity.
Shared project, session, file, and review records now carry extra context such as remotes, activity, checks, and detailed changes.

files.note: Lets session import use a server-provided project identity when present.

changes.digest: Sessions now join to one project through the shared code repository address instead of the local folder, so different machines and subfolders map together while server provided identifiers win when present, and shared data shapes now carry remote addresses, file activity, technology summaries, review checks and detailed change hunks for consistent display across tools.
